title: Design System: What Brings You In

display.purpose: Page titles and the closing "Join the reel". Mixed case only: lowercase renders as small capitals, like the logo.

headline.purpose: Section titles and titles inside detail-page hero frames.

wordmark.purpose: "What Brings You" beside the mic mark in the header (1.375rem in the footer), with a red "Brings" and the logo's script "in" as a mask.

title.purpose: The heading inside a frame. The same face at body size is the compact title in narrow frames.

lede.purpose: One introductory paragraph under a page or section title, muted, max 52ch.

body.purpose: All reading text and rendered Markdown; 66ch measure, optical sizing on.

label.purpose: Uppercase metadata printed in the film margin: stamps, counts, dates, group and field labels, follow links. Never prose.

label-plate.purpose: Button plates and primary navigation, uppercase.

numeral.purpose: Frame numbers, days and form steps, rotated -3deg, graphite; red only on a lit frame or under the team-sheet loupe.

numeral-lg.purpose: The day on the home page's next-screening frame.

shadows.name: shadow-frame
shadows.purpose: A print lying on paper: every standalone frame, the episode log, a hanging strip, the audio player.

shadows.name: shadow-lift
shadows.purpose: An interactive frame on hover, together with a 3px rise.

shadows.name: shadow-leak
shadows.purpose: Only under a hovered primary plate; the one coloured shadow.

shadows.name: field-focus
shadows.purpose: A focused text field, with the border turned red.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default curve for every state change and for the develop.

motion.name: dur-2
motion.purpose: Colour, underline and plate hover transitions.

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: Frame lift, reveal opacity and rise, shadow changes.

motion.name: dur-4
motion.purpose: The leak fading in or out; media filter on develop.

motion.name: dur-5
motion.purpose: The print darkening last as it develops; the hero logo developing.

motion.name: develop
motion.value: from opacity 0, translate 0 0.75rem, filter brightness(1.45) contrast(0.55) grayscale(0.6); opacity and translate over dur-3, filter over dur-5, ease-out
motion.purpose: Only prints (frames, or containers holding one) develop on entering the viewport. Optional stagger per group, capped at 600ms.

motion.name: ring-draw
motion.purpose: The red ring drawing itself round a lit frame's numeral once its print has developed.

motion.name: hero-title-card
motion.value: logo develops 1800ms @120ms; leak burns in 1400ms @1000ms; numeral turns red 640ms @1500ms; ring draws 1100ms @1600ms
motion.purpose: The home page's one authored moment. Static under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: xs
breakpoints.purpose: Below: the header wordmark shrinks to 1.0625rem.

breakpoints.name: sheet-2
breakpoints.purpose: Team contact sheet goes to two columns.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Two-column ledger, footer columns, horizontal episode-log frames, two hanging strips.

breakpoints.name: nav
breakpoints.purpose: At and below: primary nav collapses into the disclosure menu.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Twelve-column compositions (hero 8/4, premise, team sheet in thirds); sections open to 8rem.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: About: four hanging strips in one row.

surfaces.paper: Default page. Ink text ladder, red mark.
surfaces.beige: Archive-folder band. Paper text, mark becomes red-deep.
surfaces.stock: Graphite band and footer. On-stock text ladder, white mark, sepia-on-stock toning, color-scheme dark.
surfaces.print: Set by every Frame; resets roles to the light set whatever lies beneath.
surfaces.red: Defined in global.css, used by no page. Not part of the working system.

narrative.northStar: The Reel on the Archive Table
narrative.overview:
The site is a reel of 16mm film laid out on a McGill archive table. The page is near-white archive paper. Every episode, event, team member and statement is a white print held between graphite perforated stock. Whole sections sit in beige archive-folder bands, and the reel's tail is a closing band of graphite stock that runs straight into the footer. One McGill red, the logo's own, marks the frame that matters: it burns in from the right edge as a light leak, shows through the perforations, and comes with a red china-marker ring drawn around the frame's numeral. Prints develop out of white paper as they scroll into view. Type never moves.

The density is cozy rather than airy. Sections are 6–8rem apart and groups inside them are tight (0.75–1.5rem), so each frame reads as a dense object on an open table. Composition is loose and asymmetric: a twelve-column table with frames offset, staggered, hung at different heights or run in a strip. It is never a uniform card grid. The show's own logo is the title card. The McGill Faculty of Medicine seal (displayed with permission) appears only in the footer colophon, reversed to white. The system rejects two defaults by name: the university-template banner-crest-card-grid page, and the cream-paper, serif-headline editorial look.

The material vocabulary is literal and consistent. Perforation holes are real holes, so the surface beneath shows through them. Edge codes are printed in the film margin. Numerals are written by hand in graphite. Unfinished content is an unexposed print, and finished events are fogged and sepia-toned. Every device on the page comes from the darkroom or the contact sheet.
keyCharacteristics: White prints on near-white paper, held by graphite stock with masked perforations
One McGill red (the logo's #af2825), reserved for meaning, never laid down as a field
Four type voices with strict roles: Roman capitals, reading serif, Franklin edge codes, china-marker numerals
At most one lit frame per view: red leak plus drawn red ring
Motion only develops prints; one authored moment per page; reduced motion is fully static
Honest placeholders that look unexposed, never fake content

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: McGill red is reserved for the lit frame (leak, ring, numeral), the current page, the primary action and the brand wordmark. Beyond those four, it appears only at hairline scale: the 1px underline of an inline link, and interaction state (link hover, the focus ring, a focused field's border, a ghost plate's perforation dots on hover, the selected topic plate's 3px underline, error text). Hover and focus may also preview a frame's leak at reduced strength.

rules.name: The No Red Field Rule
rules.body: Red is never laid down as a field: no full-bleed red bands, red section backgrounds or red cards. A red surface exists in the global stylesheet but no page uses it, and new work should not start.

rules.name: The One Wordmark Red Rule
rules.body: The wordmark carries exactly one red per surface. "Brings" and the script "in" (the logo's own script, used as a mask) share it: McGill red on paper, Wordmark Red on Stock on graphite.

rules.name: The Print Resets Rule
rules.body: A frame is always a print. It resets every role token to the light set, so its contents never inherit stock or beige colours from the band it sits in.

rules.name: The Logo Capitals Rule
rules.body: Cinzel is always set in mixed case and never forced to uppercase. The small capitals are the point.

rules.name: The Edge Code Rule
rules.body: Libre Franklin uppercase is metadata only: stamps, counts, dates, labels, buttons, navigation. It never carries a sentence of prose.

rules.name: The China Marker Rule
rules.body: Caveat is used only for numerals (frame numbers, days, form steps). It is graphite at rest and turns red only when its frame is lit or held under the loupe (hover on the team sheet).

rules.name: The Print on Paper Rule
rules.body: Shadows fall down and away, warm and soft, with negative spread. There are no zero-offset glows, no grey drop shadows, and no hard offset shadows.

rules.name: The Light Leak Is Light Rule
rules.body: The red leak is light, not paint. It is a radial red gradient, multiply-blended and masked through grain and blotch textures. It sits above the print and below the rails, so ink stays ink, only the paper turns red, and the red shows through the perforations.

rules.name: The Whole Hole Rule
rules.body: Perforations always end on whole holes and always open onto the surface beneath. Never crop a rail mid-hole and never paint a hole white.

rules.name: The One Lit Frame Rule
rules.body: At most one frame is lit per view. A lit frame with a numeral always carries the drawn ring. The centred frame in a strip is only *active*: it develops but never lights.

rules.name: The Only Prints Develop Rule
rules.body: Only prints animate on scroll. Headings, ledes and action rows are type on paper and stay still, even where a reveal attribute sits on them.

dos: Do put every piece of content (an episode, event, person or premise) in a Frame: a white print between graphite rails, with its metadata in the edge code.
Do light at most one frame per view, and only one that means something (next to develop, latest, next screening, the open frame). Give it the leak at 85%, and if it has a numeral, the drawn red ring.
Do keep McGill red to the lit frame, the current page, the primary action and the wordmark, plus hairlines: link underlines, the focus ring, field focus and error text.
Do use one red per surface for the wordmark: McGill red on paper, Wordmark Red on Stock on graphite, shared by "Brings" and the script "in".
Do lay pages on archive paper, give whole sections beige folder bands, and keep graphite stock for rails, strips, plates, the closing band and the footer.
Do cut perforations with a mask, repeat them with `round` so they end on whole holes, and let the surface beneath show through.

Do keep each type voice to its role: Cinzel in mixed case for titles, Source Serif 4 for reading (66ch measure), Libre Franklin uppercase at 0.16em for metadata and controls, Caveat for numerals only.
Do keep sections 6–8rem apart and groups tight, and lay frames loose and offset on the twelve-column table.
Do keep shadows warm and falling (rgb 40 32 24, negative spread).
Do make unfinished content visibly unexposed: a beige placeholder print with a dashed sepia border and an "Add …" stamp, sepia bracketed copy, and "soon" chips.
Do develop only prints on scroll, keep one authored motion moment per page, and make reduced motion fully static.
donts: Don't lay red down as a field: no full-bleed red bands, red section backgrounds or red cards. The red surface in the global stylesheet is unused; leave it that way.
Don't use red for headings, icons, decoration or secondary actions, and don't put a second red-filled plate next to the primary.
Don't light two frames in one view, and don't light a numbered frame without its ring.
Don't animate headings, ledes or button rows, and don't add parallax or scroll-linked motion beyond the develop.
Don't paint perforation holes, crop a rail mid-hole, or let a rail sit on a surface its holes can't show.

Don't drift into the cream-paper, serif-headline editorial look: the paper is near-white and display type is the logo's Roman capitals.
Don't force Cinzel to uppercase, set prose in Libre Franklin capitals, or use Caveat for anything but numerals.
Don't round corners past 3px or use pills, and don't use zero-offset glows or grey drop shadows. The only coloured shadow is the leak under a hovered primary plate.
Don't fabricate guests, episodes, dates or counts to fill a frame. Use a latent frame or a placeholder print.
